overall: Los Angeles peaked at 75.2°F around 17:40 ET — approximately 2.1 hours ago — and has since been cooling steadily, now sitting at 71.6°F with a velocity of -1.7°F/hr. The day ran meaningfully warmer than the mostly-cloudy marine-layer setup suggested, with the observed maximum already exceeding the NWS daytime high forecast of 73°F and every NWP model's projected peak.
forecast_obs_notes: All four NWP models undershot the observed maximum: HRRR came closest at 74.7°F, followed by GFS at 73.7°F, ECMWF at 72.6°F, and NBM well below at 69.3°F — none reached the actual 75.2°F peak. The INTRADAY model's 100% concentration on the 74-75°F even bucket was the closest to reality, though the running max has now cleared even that range.
max_temp_prediction: With the day's high already observed at 75.2°F and temperatures declining for over two hours at an accelerating rate, today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 75.2°F. In the active ODD bucket market, this places the outcome in the 75-76°F odd bucket — well above the model-consensus top bucket of 71-72°F at 36.4%, representing a notable warm surprise relative to prior NWP and NWS guidance. Confidence is very high given the clear post-peak trajectory and the fact that evening cooling makes a new daily high essentially impossible.
